messages:
maya: FYI found a public gist with what looks like a base64 service account key. The gist metadata references projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/transit/cryptoKeys/transit-key. Posting minimal context here, DMing the link to leads.

kevin: Please DM me the link, don't paste the key or full gist here. Pinging ops and security.

maya: DM sent to kevin and elena. In the DM I attached a screenshot of the gist and noted the blob references that transit key path. No plaintext secrets in the public thread, just the blob.

elena: security-bot already flagged a suspicious transit/encrypt call from redwood-deploy-bot@redwood-prod on 2026-02-11T03:12:00Z. Audit id log-8a3f. I'm pulling the Vault and KMS audit trails now.

security-bot: Automated alert: outbound key usage anomaly detected for service-account redwood-deploy-bot@redwood-prod. Forensics flags: unusual client IP and new user-agent. Creating incident INC-2026-0211-TK.

opsbot: Incident play suggested: 1) revoke exposed SA creds (short-lived), 2) create new KMS key version, 3) perform canary rewrap of ciphertexts, 4) update Vault transit mapping, 5) monitor.

kevin: Ops immediate checklist (short):

``
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key transit-key --location=global --keyring=transit
# example rewrap (gcloud -> vault)
gcloud kms encrypt --key transit-key --location=global --keyring=transit --plaintext-file secret.bin --ciphertext-file secret.bin.enc
vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext=@secret.bin.enc
```

I'll prepare a script with dry-run and proceed during low-traffic windows. Will PR the script in infra.

sanjay: Priority: rotate transit key material and revoke SA tokens. Plan a staged canary rollout to avoid mass outage. Also prepare RBAC conditional deny for legacy key versions while we validate.

taylor: Proposed rollout: 1) create new key version, 2) re-encrypt small canary set (non-customer critical), 3) point vault-transit to new key version, 4) monitor errors and latency, 5) expand. Add automated rollback if error rate exceeds 0.5%. I'll wire alerts to PagerDuty for >0.2% errors during the rollout.

kevin: PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1824 contains rewrap script + dry-run output. Starting canary on canary-1 in ~10m.

elena: Audit steps: enable object-level KMS audit logging, ensure Vault audit device to external syslog (90d retention), collect token-level traces from runtimes to map ciphertext IDs to services.

maya: Question: do we switch to KMS-wrapped keys only, or keep KMS + Vault-transit hybrid? My preference: hybrid to minimize runtime changes.

taylor: Hybrid makes sense. Use KMS as root wrap and keep transit as the interface layer so rollbacks are easier.

kevin: Running canary-1 now (staging canary). Script has dry-run and live modes. Will post results here.

elena: Forensics update: no decrypt/plaintext exfil observed so far; only encrypt calls from the exposed SA. Still treating as credential exposure and rotating keys. Mapping affected ciphertexts to services now.

kevin: Canary-1 ran 15m with zero errors. Rolling to canary-2 in prod subset.

sanjay: RBAC tweak example to temporary deny legacy access during grace period:

``
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding transit-key --member='serviceAccount:redwood-deploy-bot@redwood-prod' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' --condition="expression=request.time < timestamp('2026-02-11T05:00:00Z')"
```

We'll tighten down after validation.

opsbot: Remember to rotate any long-lived secrets that the SA could have accessed, issue OIDC ephemeral creds, and document the exact timeline in the incident.

maya: Owners: kevin=rewrap & rollout, elena=audits & forensics, sanjay=RBAC + revoke, taylor=monitoring & canary validation. ETA: initial canary started ~2 hours after discovery. Postmortem will follow.

kevin: Canary-2 completed with acceptable metrics. Scheduling bulk rewrap script to run in windows overnight. Script supports dry-run, parallelism control, and a verification step comparing ciphertext fingerprints.

elena: Forensics: created mapping of ciphertext IDs -> services -> tenant impact. Prioritizing customer-facing production services first for rewrap.

sanjay: After bulk rollout, follow-ups: 1) run full credential inventory to find other possible exposures, 2) add DLP checks for public paste sites for known patterns, 3) incorporate detection rule to alert on unusual key usage patterns.

maya: Agreed. If any canary step shows >0.5% errors, abort and rollback. Posting a short postmortem doc and linking to INC-2026-0211-TK when complete. Thanks all.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-0211-TK updated with owners, timeline, and links to PR and runbook. Next status update in 30m or on major change.
